---
title: "Frequentist OC timing: BExTE and RBesT"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Frequentist OC timing: BExTE and RBesT}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

This benchmark times one frequentist operating-characteristic (OC) calculation
for a normal treatment-effect estimate. It compares BExTE's simulation-based
`oc_frequentist()` with RBesT's integration-based `oc1S()`. The two calls use
the same analysis prior, sampling standard error, decision threshold, and true
effects. They use different algorithms and return different amounts of detail:
BExTE also reports bias, mean squared error, and coverage. These timings
describe this task on this machine, not a general speed ranking.
BExTE's RMP implementation itself uses RBesT for mixture updates; the timing
difference here is primarily between the two OC workflows.

Other comparisons are possible, but I have not validated an equivalent OC
calculation for these package pairs:

| Package | Candidate common setup | Difference to resolve before timing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hdbayes` | Fixed power prior for source and target two-arm binary data (`glm.pp()` in hdbayes; `power_prior()` in BExTE) | Align the initial prior and treatment-effect scale: a logit-link GLM coefficient differs from BExTE's exact-binomial risk difference. |
| `NPP` | Normalised power prior for historical and current Bernoulli data (`BerNPP_MCMC()`; BExTE's `npp()`) | NPP's documented Bernoulli function models one response probability; BExTE's binomial NPP models a two-arm treatment effect. |
| `psborrow2` | Two-arm binary trial with historical controls and a commensurate prior | psborrow2 borrows external control-arm outcomes; BExTE's `commensurate_prior()` borrows a source treatment effect. |

These are candidates for separate workflow benchmarks. They do not yet support
an identical-model speed ratio.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(BExTE)
library(RBesT)
```

## Matched scenario

The source study has 50 patients per arm, estimated treatment effect 0.2,
and standard error 0.1. With `rmp(weight = 0.5)`, BExTE's analysis prior is
`0.5 N(0.2, 0.1^2) + 0.5 N(0, 0.5)`. The target trial also has 50 patients
per arm, giving a treatment-effect sampling standard error of 0.1. We evaluate
the null boundary (true effect 0) and an alternative (true effect 0.2). Success
means `Pr(effect > 0 | data) > 0.975`.

```{r scenario}
src <- source_data(n_control = 50, n_treatment = 50,
                   estimate = 0.2, se = 0.1)
bexte_prior <- rmp(src, weight = 0.5)
bexte_decision <- decision(critical_value = 0.975)

rbest_prior <- RBesT::mixnorm(
  info = c(0.5, 0.2, 0.1),
  vague = c(0.5, 0, sqrt(0.5)),
  sigma = sqrt(0.5)
)
rbest_decision <- RBesT::decision1S(pc = 0.975, qc = 0,
                                     lower.tail = FALSE)
true_effects <- c(0, 0.2)
```

## Timing

Each BExTE call simulates 1,000 target trials per true effect. RBesT computes
the OC function by integration, so it has no simulation count. Priors and
decision rules are prepared before timing. Both functions run once to warm up
loaded code. The table reports the median of three BExTE calls and three
batches of 100 RBesT calls; each RBesT batch is divided by 100 to get the
time per two-effect OC calculation. The calls run sequentially in one R
process.

```{r benchmark}
run_bexte <- function() {
  as.data.frame(oc_frequentist(
    bexte_prior, bexte_decision, n_per_arm = 50,
    drift = c(-0.2, 0), n_rep = 1000
  ))
}
run_rbest <- function() {
  design <- RBesT::oc1S(rbest_prior, n = 50,
                        decision = rbest_decision, sigma = sqrt(0.5))
  design(true_effects)
}

set.seed(20261012)
bexte_oc <- run_bexte()
rbest_oc <- run_rbest()

bexte_seconds <- replicate(3, {
  set.seed(20261012)
  unname(system.time(run_bexte())[["elapsed"]])
})
rbest_seconds <- replicate(3, {
  unname(system.time(for (i in seq_len(100)) run_rbest())[["elapsed"]]) / 100
})

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(bexte_oc$true_effect, true_effects)))
stopifnot(all(abs(bexte_oc$success_proba - rbest_oc) < 0.05))
comparison <- data.frame(
  Package = c("BExTE", "RBesT"),
  Algorithm = c("Monte Carlo (1,000 trials/effect)", "Numerical integration"),
  `Median elapsed (s)` = round(c(median(bexte_seconds),
                                 median(rbest_seconds)), 3),
  `Type I error` = round(c(bexte_oc$success_proba[1], rbest_oc[1]), 3),
  Power = round(c(bexte_oc$success_proba[2], rbest_oc[2]), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(comparison)
```

The OC estimates should be close, within Monte Carlo uncertainty. Elapsed
times will vary with hardware, package versions, and system load. To report a
new timing, render this vignette on the target machine and copy its table and
session details into the README.

```{r environment}
cat("R:", as.character(getRversion()), "\n")
cat("BExTE:", as.character(packageVersion("BExTE")), "\n")
cat("RBesT:", as.character(packageVersion("RBesT")), "\n")
cat("Platform:", R.version$platform, "\n")
cat("OS:", Sys.info()[["sysname"]], Sys.info()[["release"]], "\n")
```
